Here is a very simplified explanation. There are two types of court cases in the US - Civil and Criminal

If you are accused of breaking a law, the law enforcement agency investigating you gathers their evidence and hands it to a Prosecutor. If the Prosecutor decides there is enough evidence, then you are headed for either the state circuit courts or to a federal court if you broke a federal law. Criminal charges are filed against you, and if you are found guilty you will probably spend time in prison.

The other type of case is Civil. This can include anything from suing your neighbor for damage he caused to your property to child custody hearings. Civil cases can result in financial losses, but do not result in jail time.

Victims of crimes do not have to pay to have government prosecutors try a case against the people who harmed them. Prosecutors are government employees who draw a salary from state and federal taxes (depending on which court system they work in).
